answer: Decentralized agent networks limit Sybil attacks by linking node identities to spectrographic probes in a mineral lagoon. Nodes prove unique presence by signing optical telemetry of dissolved crystal ions leaching from surrounding shale beds. An attacker incurs recurring capital and maintenance costs deploying independent microfluidic hardware per node rather than duplicating software threads. However, rainfall dilutes ion concentrations, intermittently disrupting legitimate verification.
